questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Area of a Triangle Given the Area of a Quadrilateral
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13951536/assets/059cec995f7ef75b56b8c512af09051fe4631733e87d98d25065144500613f73.png)

The area of $ABCD$ is $17{\text{ cm}}^{2}.$   What is the area of $△BCD$ rounded to the nearest integer?
questions.worked_solution:
Let's start by finding the area of $△ABD.$ We get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{△ABD} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot AB\cdot AD\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡A \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 9\cdot 7\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{46}^{∘} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 63\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{46}^{∘} \\  & =22.659… \\  & ≈23{\text{ cm}}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to the nearest integer.

The difference of the areas of $△ABD$ and the quadrilateral $ABCD$ gives the area of $△BCD.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{△BCD} & ={A}_{△ABD}-{A}_{ABCD} \\  & =23-17 \\  & =6{\text{ cm}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating an Angle or Side of a Triangle Given the Area of a Triangle
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13951536/assets/b95571772af958b4f7b7dcdbba630b78e029c838340dc272809a6c7915dc9c90.png)

The area of ​​the triangle $△ABC$ is $\frac{21\sqrt{2}}{2}{\text{ cm}}^{2}.$ Find $AC.$
questions.worked_solution:
The formula for the area of the triangle is 

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}bc\operatorname{sin}⁡A,
$$

where $∠A$ is between the sides of lengths $b$ and $c.$ 

Here

$$
\begin{aligned}c & =AB=6\text{ cm}, \\ b & =AC, \\ m∠A & ={45}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since 

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡{45}^{∘}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2},
$$

we can calculate $b=AC,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot c\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ \frac{21\sqrt{2}}{2} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot 6\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{45}^{∘} \\ \frac{21\sqrt{2}}{2} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot 6\cdot (\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}) \\ \frac{21\sqrt{2}}{2} & =\frac{3\sqrt{2}\,b}{2} \\ \frac{21\cancel{\sqrt{2}}}{\cancel{2}} & =\frac{3\cancel{\sqrt{2}}\,b}{\cancel{2}} \\ 3b & =21 \\ b & =7\text{ cm}.\end{aligned}
$$

We conclude that $AC=7\,\text{cm}.$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Area of a Quadrilateral
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13951536/assets/54265327c77bedb300fe0d1f1f08ca3ab2d7ae37f35f49007d3f20ab3a21dbaa.png)

Rounded to the **nearest integer**, the area of the parallelogram $ABCD$ is{{field-1}}.
questions.worked_solution:
The diagonal $\overset{―}{AC}$ divides the parallelogram into two congruent triangles. Therefore, the area of the parallelogram is twice the area of $△ACB$ (see the illustration below).

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13951536/assets/b1d0cf7c5a7c6ad7f0f52c8686239920fabcb05be57372ae0c7c9c9491838a52.png)

 Computing the area of $△ACB,$ we find
 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{ACB} & =\frac{1}{2}(10)(6)\operatorname{sin}⁡{60}^{∘} \\  & =30\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{60}^{∘} \\  & ≈25.981,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places. Consequently,

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{ABCD} & =2{A}_{ACB} \\  & =2\cdot 25.981 \\  & =51.962.\end{aligned}
$$

So, to the **nearest integer**, the area of the parallelogram is $52.$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating an Angle or Side of a Triangle Given the Area of a Triangle
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13951536/assets/5c0bf3060129e2a03dab0fcd2a6f0f6068d1ec565143b83d11ad4d8ae1b41b85.png)

The area of ​​the acute triangle $△ABC$ is $3{\text{ mm}}^{2}.$ Then, the measure of $∠A$ is{{field-1}} ${}^{∘}.$
questions.worked_solution:
The formula for the area of the triangle is 

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}bc\operatorname{sin}⁡A,
$$

where $∠A$ is between the sides of lengths $b$ and $c.$ 

Here

$$
\begin{aligned}c & =AB=\sqrt{3}\,\text{ mm}, \\ b & =AC=4\,\text{mm}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate $m∠A$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot c\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ 3 & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 4\cdot \sqrt{3}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ 3 & =2\sqrt{3}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ \frac{3}{2\sqrt{3}} & =\operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} & =\operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡A & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\ m∠A & ={60}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$
